title: Platform credit reclamation and expiry protocol — operator handbook
author: Aisha Chen
content:
Overview
This handbook defines the platform-level protocol for reclaiming, expiring, and reconciling customer credits and free-tier entitlements that interact with Redwood’s multi-tenant inference platform. It covers monitoring dashboards, automated reclaiming policies, manual operator procedures, post-action retrospectives, and roadmap actions to reduce operator friction and customer impact.

Scope
- Applies to hosted API credits (free trial credits, promo credits, and partner grants) and platform-level burst credits allocated to tenants.
- Does NOT cover enterprise reserved capacity contractual billing reconciliations (see finance playbook).
- Operators, platform engineers, and billing on-call are primary audiences.

Definitions
- Credit balance: token/embedding unit balance in tenant account metadata.
- Expiry window: 90 days by default for promotional credits unless overridden by contract.
- Reclamation: automated recovery of unused ephemeral credits assigned for experiments or platform grants.

Principles
- Avoid user-visible surprise: reclaim only after notifications and grace period.
- Safety first: automated reclaiming must pass checks to ensure not affecting live requests.
- Observable & auditable: every reclaim action must be logged, reversible where possible, and surfaced in dashboards.

Monitoring and dashboards
- Primary dashboard: "Credit Lifecycle Monitor" (dashboard id: PLAT-CR-001) shows:
  - Active promo credits by expiry bucket (0–7d, 8–30d, 31–90d, >90d)
  - Reclaim candidate queue size and processing latency
  - Reclaim errors (permission, tenant-state, API failures)
  - Customer-impact indicator: number of requests failed with "insufficient credits" in last 24h once reclaim runs

- Alerting thresholds (PagerDuty -> Platform Billing):
  1) reclaim-error-rate > 1% over 10m -> SEV3
  2) number of customers with failed requests after reclaim > 5 in 15m -> SEV2
  3) reclaim-backlog > 10k tenant-credits for >4h -> warn

Reclaim automation overview
1) Candidate selection (daily): rules engine selects credits approaching expiry, credits tagged as ephemeral, or promo grants flagged by finance. Exclusion rules: active dedicated tenants, active enterprise contracts, flagged disputes.
2) Notification phase (48h prior to scheduled reclaim): customers receive email + in-console banner with action link. Notifications use templated messages with link to extend or consume credits.
3) Soft lock (24h): platform marks credits as "pending_reclaim" — no automatic usage for new allocations but existing in-flight requests continue.
4) Reclaim window (scheduled job): background job attempts reclaim via billing API; successful reclaims transition credit state to "reclaimed" and emit audit event.
5) Post-reclaim reconciliation: nightly batch runs to reconcile reclaimed credits with billing ledger.

Operator runbook: automated reclaim failure (step-by-step)
1) Detection
   - Observe PLAT-CR-001 dashboard and reclaim-error alert or SEV pager.
2) Initial verification (5–15 min)
   - Check reclaim job logs: /logs/cron/reclaim-YYYYMMDD (GCS path shown in dashboard).
   - Query failing tenant IDs: SQL snippet below.
3) Immediate mitigation (if >1% error rate or customer-failures)
   - Pause reclaim pipeline: CLI -> platformctl reclaim pause --reason "operator-sev" --until <RFC3339>
   - Post temporary banner on status page and update incident in PagerDuty runbook page.
4) Root cause triage (15–60 min)
   - Common causes checklist: API auth expiring, billing ledger write-back failure, db transaction deadlock, quota service returning 5xx.
   - Use trace ID from logs to correlate with request path in APM (APM tag: reclaim.job).
5) Recovery
   - If transient (quota service outage): resume reclaim and monitor 30m.
   - If permanent or ambiguous: rollback partial reclaims using audit events: platformctl reclaim rollback --from <timestamp> --tenant-ids <list>.
6) Post-incident tasks
   - Create retrospective ticket with timeline + operator actions (template below).

Manual reconciliation procedure (when reclaim automation is paused or for disputed cases)
1) Validate dispute: confirm customer support ticket references tenant id and credit grant id.
2) Inspect tenant usage: run queries for last 90 days, check active model endpoints and dedicated capacity.
3) Apply manual adjustments: billing_ui -> Adjust credits -> record adjustment reason and attach support ticket id.
4) Audit: add line item to ledger: INSERT INTO billing.reconciliation_log (...). Store copy in GCS archive /reconciliations/<date>/manual-<tenant>.json.

CLI/SQL examples
- Query reclaim candidates:
  SELECT tenant_id, grant_id, expires_at, balance FROM platform.promo_credits WHERE expires_at BETWEEN now() AND now() + interval '7 days' AND state = 'active';
- Pause reclaim pipeline:
  platformctl reclaim pause --reason "operator-sev" --until 2026-01-11T09:00:00Z

Audit table example (text)
| timestamp | tenant_id | action | actor | reference_id | notes |
| 2026-01-09T02:14:00Z | t-12345 | reclaim | system-cron | grant-987 | automated reclaim after notification |

Safety checklist before any mass reclaim (>1000 tenants)
- Confirm notifications were sent and delivery rates > 95% (notification-service dashboard).
- Confirm grace periods and contract exceptions list.
- Ensure nightly ledger reconciliation jobs are green.
- Run dry-run in canary namespace and verify no failed requests.

Retrospective and tuning notes (living section)
- Recent retrospective (2025-11-20): mass reclaim caused 12 customer support escalations due to missing exclusion tag for partner grants. Actions: add partner_grant flag to rule and require finance sign-off for >10k credit reclaims.
- Tuning recommendations: increase notification window to 72h for promo credits > $500 equivalent; add rate-limited reclaim waves to avoid peaks.

Roadmap items (priority order)
1) Q2 2026: Automatic dispute hold integration — allow support tickets to place a temporary hold on reclaim candidates.
2) Q3 2026: Fine-grained tenant simulation — run synthetic workload during dry-runs to surface failures.
3) Q4 2026: Per-tenant reclaim policy UI in Console (ops + finance only).
4) 2027: Cross-region reclamation consistency checks and ledger replication to avoid double-reclaims.

Metrics and SLOs
- Reclaim success rate: target 99.5% per nightly job.
- Notification delivery: 99% within 1 hour of send job.
- Reconciliation latency: ledger must reflect reclaim events within 1 hour (95th percentile).

Ownership and escalation
- Primary owner: Billing Platform Team (oncall roster -> billing-platform).
- Secondary: Platform Operators (oncall).
- If SEV2/SEV1: page via PagerDuty escalation chain (billing-platform -> eng-sre -> exec oncall).

Appendix: incident retrospective template (copy/paste)
1) Title & timeframe
2) Summary (one paragraph)
3) Timeline of events (with timestamps)
4) Root cause analysis
5) Operator actions taken (what worked/what didn’t)
6) Customer impact and support count
7) Follow-ups and owner assignments

Appendix: quick reference links
- Dashboard: PLAT-CR-001 (internal link)
- Reclaim job logs: gs://redwood-logs/reclaim/
- Reconciliation ledger schema: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts/ledger-spec-2024

Document maintenance
- Reviewed quarterly by Billing Platform and Platform Operators.
- Major changes require finance and legal sign-off if policy or expiry window is altered.
